issues.t: Airbag light on from water in crash sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays lit on the dash.
issues.why: The housing of the front crash-zone sensor can crack and let water in, shorting the sensor so the airbags may not work in a crash. Mazda recalled 2004 cars to inspect and replace the sensor.
issues.next: Run your VIN through a recall lookup. An airbag light that stays on means the airbags may be switched off, so get it diagnosed promptly.

issues.t: Steering wheel emblem can break apart when airbag deploys (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving. The danger only shows up if the driver airbag goes off.
issues.why: The Mazda emblem on the driver airbag cover can shatter when the airbag deploys and send sharp pieces toward the driver. Mazda recalled these cars to replace the cover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the airbag cover replaced at a Mazda dealer as soon as possible.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly turns very heavy, sometimes with a whine from the steering pump, most often at low speed or while parking.
issues.why: The electric-hydraulic power steering pump on cars built in this window can lose assist. Mazda recalled these cars and replaced the pump and lines.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the steering goes heavy, drive slowly and carefully to a shop and get it repaired before regular driving.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers work slowly or on and off, then stop completely.
issues.why: A ground terminal on the wiper motor can bend and lose contact over time. Mazda recalled these cars and added a ground wire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Do not drive in rain or snow with wipers that quit; get the recall repair done first.

issues.t: Check engine light from a rubbed-through air/fuel sensor wire
issues.sym: Check engine light comes on with codes such as P0131 or P2251; the car may otherwise feel normal.
issues.why: The wiring for the front air/fuel ratio sensor can rub against a nearby bracket and wear through. Mazda described the check and repair in a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have the sensor harness inspected before replacing parts. A damaged sensor or harness should be repaired so fuel economy and emissions stay normal.

issues.t: Worn or broken engine mounts
issues.sym: Clunking when you shift into drive or reverse, heavy vibration at idle that you feel in the seat and steering wheel, or a thump when you get on and off the gas.
issues.why: The rubber engine and transmission mounts, especially the upper mount, can crack or tear with age and mileage, letting the engine move around more than it should.
issues.next: Have a mechanic check the mounts with the hood open while someone shifts between drive and reverse. Replace any torn mount before it puts extra strain on axles, hoses and the exhaust.

issues.t: Sticky, shiny dashboard top
issues.sym: The top of the dash turns tacky or glossy, picks up dust and lint, and throws a bright glare onto the windshield on sunny days.
issues.why: The dash pad material on cars built from late 2008 to spring 2010 can break down in heat and humidity. Mazda extended coverage for the sticky surface, but that extension has now expired on every eligible car.
issues.next: A sunshade slows it down. If the glare makes it hard to see out, a replacement dash pad or a fitted dash cover is the practical fix. Ask a dealer whether any goodwill help is still offered.

issues.t: Early clutch wear on manual cars
issues.sym: The clutch slips when you accelerate hard, the engine revs without the car speeding up, the pedal feels soft or sticks, or the car is hard to get into gear.
issues.why: Manual-transmission cars from these years drew many reports of clutches wearing out far earlier than expected, often well before typical clutch life.
issues.next: Have a shop check the clutch and the hydraulic master and slave cylinders. If the clutch is replaced, have the hydraulics inspected at the same time.

issues.t: Driver seat rocks back and forth (recall)
issues.sym: The driver seat feels loose and rocks or tilts, especially when you shift your weight or brake.
issues.why: On seats with a manual height lever, the lifter links can break or come loose from the seat frame. Mazda recalled these cars and added a reinforcing bracket or a new adjuster.
issues.next: Run your VIN through a recall lookup. If the seat rocks, have the free recall repair done soon, since a loose seat is a crash safety concern.

issues.t: Hatch struts can corrode and let the liftgate drop (recall)
issues.sym: The rear hatch will not stay up on its own, sinks slowly, or drops suddenly.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold up the liftgate on hatchbacks can rust and break. Mazda recalled these cars to replace both struts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Until it is fixed, hold or prop the hatch when loading so it cannot fall on anyone.

issues.t: Oil leak and rattle from the drive belt tensioner
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, mostly when accelerating, and oily residue around the belt tensioner.
issues.why: The hydraulic auto-tensioner for the drive belt on the 2.0L Skyactiv engine can leak its oil and lose damping, letting the belt flap. Mazda issued a bulletin covering the leak and noise.
issues.next: Have the tensioner and belt inspected. Replace a leaking tensioner before the belt slips or comes off, which would cut charging and engine cooling.

issues.t: Mazda Connect screen ghost touches, freezes or reboots
issues.sym: The touchscreen selects things on its own, freezes, keeps rebooting, goes blank, drops Bluetooth or navigation, or the backup camera picture does not appear.
issues.why: The early Mazda Connect system can register false touches and its software can get stuck in a reboot loop. Mazda issued several service bulletins, and a class action settlement extended coverage on these units.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to update the software and check whether the settlement warranty extension applies to your car. Unplug aftermarket accessories to rule them out. A screen that keeps acting on its own usually needs replacement.

issues.t: No-start, battery drain or odd electrical faults linked to accessories
issues.sym: The car intermittently will not start, the security light flashes, the battery runs down overnight, or the backup camera picture blurs.
issues.why: Mazda found that plug-in chargers, dash cams, GPS units and other aftermarket devices can upset the electrical system on these cars, and issued bulletins telling technicians to check for them first.
issues.next: Unplug all aftermarket devices and see if the problem stops. If it continues, have the battery, charging system and wiring connections tested.

issues.t: Alternator belt can slip in heavy rain (recall)
issues.sym: The battery or charging light comes on while driving in heavy rain, and electrical items may start to fail.
issues.why: Water can make the alternator belt slip, so the battery stops charging and the car can eventually lose power. Mazda reprogrammed the engine computer to fix it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the reprogramming done. If the charging light comes on, get off the road safely before the battery runs flat.

issues.t: Parking brake can rust and stick (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake does not fully release, the rear brakes drag or get hot, or the parking brake does not hold well.
issues.why: Water can get into the rear calipers and corrode the parking brake actuator shaft so it binds. Mazda recalled these cars to inspect and replace corroded shafts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Have the rear brakes checked right away if they drag or the parking brake will not hold.

issues.t: Fuel tank weld can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the rear of the car or drips under the fuel tank.
issues.why: Some fuel tanks were damaged or poorly welded at the factory, and a weld near the fill check valve can fail and leak. Mazda recalled affected cars to inspect and replace tanks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you smell fuel or see a leak, do not drive the car; have it inspected because leaking fuel is a fire risk.

issues.t: Fuel shut-off valve can cause leak or stall (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, a check engine light, rough running, or the engine stalling after a fill-up.
issues.why: A faulty shut-off valve in the fuel tank can let liquid fuel into the evaporative emissions system, which can lead to a fuel leak or a stall. Owners were told not to drive until it was repaired.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and do not drive the car until the recall repair is done.

issues.t: Backup camera picture flickers or distorts (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera image flickers, is distorted, or does not show when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the camera and its connector. Mazda recalled these cars to replace the camera and seal the harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Until it is fixed, check around the car with mirrors and over your shoulder before backing up.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers work on and off or stop entirely.
issues.why: A faulty wiper relay inside the front body control module can fail. Mazda recalled these cars to replace the module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Do not drive in rain or snow if the wipers act up; get the repair done first.

issues.t: Wrong exhaust valve spring can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Some engines were built with an incorrect exhaust valve spring that can break. Mazda recalled affected cars to inspect and replace parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have it fixed promptly, since a stall in traffic is dangerous.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, rough running, a check engine light, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The impeller inside the low-pressure fuel pump can crack and stop the pump. Mazda recalled affected cars to replace the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and get the pump replaced. A stall at speed is a safety risk.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates for no reason (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly brakes hard with nothing in the way, usually while driving normally.
issues.why: The Smart Brake Support system can wrongly detect an obstacle. Mazda updated the software and replaced or updated the instrument cluster on some cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the update done right away. Until then, stay alert for sudden braking and ask the dealer about switching the system off.

issues.t: Engine may stall while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or at idle, often with warning lights, and may then restart.
issues.why: A programming error in the engine computer could cause a stall. Mazda reprogrammed affected cars under a recall that also covered some Mazda6 and CX-5 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the engine computer reprogrammed. A stall in traffic is dangerous, so do not put this off.

issues.t: Lug nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a wheel, vibration, or a wobble that gets worse with speed.
issues.why: Lug nuts on some cars may not have been tightened correctly and can work loose, which could let a wheel come off. Mazda recalled them to retighten the nuts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you hear clunking from a wheel, stop and check the lug nuts before driving further.

issues.t: Front head restraint may not lock in place (recall)
issues.sym: The front headrest moves down or does not click into its raised position.
issues.why: Seat fabric can get in the way of the headrest lock. Mazda recalled affected cars to add spacers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. A headrest that will not lock gives less protection in a rear crash, so get it fixed.

issues.t: Check engine light from cylinder deactivation fault
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P3400, sometimes with rough running.
issues.why: The 2.5L engine shuts off two cylinders when cruising. Mazda issued a bulletin for a fault in that system and later released a new cylinder head assembly for repairs.
issues.next: Have the code read at a Mazda dealer and ask about the cylinder deactivation bulletin. Do not ignore it if the engine runs rough or the light flashes.

issues.t: Front brake caliper bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling from a front wheel, especially when braking, or a change in how the brakes feel.
issues.why: Some caliper bolts may not have been tightened enough at the factory and can work loose, reducing braking. Mazda recalled affected cars to check and tighten them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you hear clunking from the front brakes, stop driving and have them inspected.

issues.t: Tire valve stems can suddenly leak (recall)
issues.sym: A tire loses air quickly and the tire pressure warning light comes on.
issues.why: Some tire valves were faulty and can start leaking without warning. Mazda recalled affected cars to replace all four valves.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the tire pressure light comes on, slow down and check the tires before continuing.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or shows no camera image when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software error can stop camera images from displaying. Mazda recalled affected cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Back up carefully using mirrors until the update is done.

issues.t: Forward camera fault disables emergency braking (recall)
issues.sym: Warning messages about driver-assist systems, and automatic emergency braking or lane keeping not working.
issues.why: The forward sensing camera can fail and switch off the emergency braking and lane-keep systems. Mazda recalled affected cars to inspect and replace the camera.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Drive as if those safety systems are off until the camera is fixed.

issues.t: Airbag sensor can switch off the airbags (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, often after the battery has been run down.
issues.why: A low-battery condition can make the airbag sensor unit log an error and turn the airbags off. Mazda recalled the Mazda3 and CX-30 to reprogram or replace the sensor.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the airbag light is on, the airbags may not deploy, so get the repair done promptly.
